note: Source-linked international HYROX briefings. Publication dates are used where available; undated official pages are labelled Checked. Reviewed 25 October 2026.

items.title: The Elite Series heads from Hamburg to Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon
items.summary: The 2026/27 official schedule opens in Hamburg on 30–31 October, followed by London, Bangkok, Las Vegas and Lyon. Elite 15 and Challenger 15 races share the stage, with the series building towards Hong Kong 2027.

items.title: Singapore, Melbourne and Hong Kong: away-race options for the new season
items.summary: The official calendar lists Singapore on 26–29 November, Melbourne on 9–13 December and Hong Kong on 7–10 January. Compare the race dates with travel and recovery time before choosing your next start line.

items.title: Stockholm: Australia defends its mixed-relay world title
items.summary: PUMA's World Championships report records Australia's mixed-relay win in 50:19, with Jess Pettrow part of the title-defending team. Joanna Wietrzyk also finished second in the women's Elite 15 solo race.

items.title: Elite qualification switches to a rolling points system
items.summary: HYROX's 2026/27 framework uses results over a rolling 365-day window: the best five singles results or best three doubles results count. Elite Series doubles partners must share the same nationality, and an active athlete licence is required.

items.title: Hong Kong to host the 2027 World Championships
items.summary: HYROX announced that the World Championships will reach the Asia-Pacific region for the first time, at Hong Kong's AsiaWorld-Expo on 10–13 June 2027. The announcement puts an international target on next season's qualification journey.

items.title: Project Podium opens a new route to athlete support
items.summary: PUMA announced a programme offering men's, women's and adaptive solo podium finishers at the 2026 World Championships the chance to become PUMA athletes for the following season. The offer includes kit, training resources and performance support.
